SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 20, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
NOVEMBER 20, 2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery from The Church of Jesus
  Christ of Latter-Day Saints.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by City of Cerritos Recreation Services “Joy of
  Singing” class member Isabell Jones.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  A proclamation was presented to:

  Orchard Supply Hardware (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Armin Reyes thanked the City Council and City Manager on behalf of the Cerritos
  High School boy’s water polo team, parents, coaches, and staff for their quick
  response in providing seating for the opposing team at their CIF championship
  game.

  Jeffery Park, co-ed coach Cerritos High School water polo, thanked the Mayor,
  City Council, City Manager and staff for assisting the Cerritos High School water
  polo team.

  Danny Shafik thanked the Mayor, City Council, City Manager and staff for
  assisting the Cerritos High School water polo team.

  Cerritos High School water polo team presented flowers to thank the Mayor, City
  Council, City Manager and staff.

  Scott Smith, President and CEO of the Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce,
  presented “Shop Small Saturday” shopping bags to the City Council and
  encouraged shoppers to shop small businesses on Saturday.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding the City noise ordinance, public comment time
  limits, Neighborhood Watch, and AB 109.

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning/Economic

  Paul W. Bellenbaum requested clarification of whether both medical and
  commercial marijuana will be prohibited in the City of Cerritos.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full reading of
  and introduce Ordinance No. 1018, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of potential changes to the City’s General Municipal
  Election date in light of recent legislation (Senate Bills 415, 450, and 568) and
  other related factors (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk. A PowerPoint Presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding an additional option of back to back elections that
  would not increase or decrease current Council member terms, but reduce terms
  to 3 years and 7 months for newly elected members.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke in opposition of the City’s possible participation in
  SB 415 litigation and recommended the City abide by the Attorney General’s
  Opinion on SB 415.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:
  1. Present a resolution at the December 14, 2017 regular City Council meeting
  to adopt a Cerritos California Voter Rights Participation Act Compliance Plan
  to consolidate future General Municipal Elections with a California statewide
  primary or statewide general election commencing with the statewide
  primary election to be held on March 3, 2020 or no later than the statewide
  general election to be held November 8, 2022, and
  2. Introduce an ordinance to change the City’s General Municipal Election date
  from the second Tuesday of April in odd-numbered years to the first Tuesday
  after the first Monday in March in even-numbered years commencing March
  3, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4-1, Solanki “No”) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
